author: United States Navy
title: Duty-assignment entries for John Charles Tashner Jr., October 1943 – April 1945
notes:
Two duty entries for J. C. Tashner Jr., supplied by his grandson in August 2026 as text and filed at the primary rung because of what they are by form: service papers, in the flat register of a duty record rather than the register of a recollection. "Serviced PBY and Army B24 Aircraft - emergency repair. In charge of maintenance crew detachment on Island of Betio." And: "Chief radioman in charge of electronics division fleet plane pool at Majuro, G.I. Readying aircraft for fleet and preserving aircraft for overhaul." The dates given with them are October 1943 – May 1944 and May 1944 – April 1945.

**The provenance is thin and that is part of the citation.** This project has seen the text and not the paper. There is no scan, no photograph, no NARA or National Personnel Records Center reference, and no statement of which document the entries were copied from — a service record, a transfer sheet, a fitness report or a summary made from them. Nobody here has established that the entries say what they are said to say, and filing them at `primary` is a judgement about their form, not a verification. Cite them as duty entries transcribed by the family, which is how the 1941 pack cites them; the reason they are not filed at `testimony` is docs/sources.md's rule that a work is filed by its form, with the doubts written into `notes` instead of into the tier.

Two things about the text itself. Only the double-quoted spans above are presented as record wording; the surrounding dates and the sentence "Invasion of Tarawa Island took place in November. He was there" arrived as the family's framing around them, and this pack keeps that boundary. And the record abbreviates: it says "Majuro, G.I.", which the transcription expands to "Majuro, Gilbert Islands". Majuro is in the Marshall Islands; Betio and Tarawa are in the Gilberts. The expansion may be the transcriber's and the abbreviation may be a clerk's, and this project asserts neither — see the note on the Person entry.

What the entries are good for: that Jay Tashner's war after Pearl Harbor was aviation ground support and electronics rather than deck service, which corroborates his son's account from a documentary direction; that he was a chief radioman by 1944; and that he was on Betio and at Majuro in those windows. What they are not good for: any date inside a range, and in particular whether he was on Betio during the assault of 20–23 November 1943 or after it.
